az_stupa_crag.blurb: A small wall in the Chimney Rock Area on the west side of Sedona, with about a dozen climbs: ten sport lines, one trad route and one set up for top rope. Grades run from 5.6 up to a single 5.11, but most fall between 5.7 and 5.10, so beginners and intermediate climbers both find something. The walk from the trailhead is short, around five minutes, and the setting has good views over the red rock country. Most lines face south or southwest. Expect loose flakes along the tops and sides of routes, and wear a helmet.

az_girlie_man_area.blurb: A compact, mixed granite crag in the McDowell Mountains of northeast Scottsdale, reached from the Tom's Thumb trailhead. Twelve climbs share the area: a handful of bolted slabs, some trad cracks, and a couple of boulder problems. Technical grades are mostly easy to moderate, from low fifth class through 5.9, with the bouldering sitting at the easy end of the V scale. The rough desert granite rewards good footwork on the slabs and clean jamming on the cracks. A short scramble leads to the base, and the setting suits a relaxed half day near the city.

az_1_pawn_chessapeak.blurb: The first sector of the Chessman Area in Bear Canyon on Mt Lemmon, north of Tucson. A dozen routes, split between trad and bolted lines, cover a broad range from 5.6 up to a pair at 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The main wall looks south and picks up sun nearly all day, which makes it a better cool-weather choice than a summer one. Getting there takes some effort: a scrambly walk up a rocky drainage, then a faint path along the cliff base.
az_1_pawn_chessapeak.approach: From the roadside pullout, hike straight up the rocky drainage with some light scrambling, take the uphill left branch where it forks near the cliff, pass the Queen sector, then follow a faint trail left along the base.

az_wind_wall.blurb: A short wall tucked just below the Windy Point overlook on Mt Lemmon, near Tucson. Twelve sport and trad lines can all be top-roped from chain anchors, and the grades cluster around 5.10 with some 5.9 and 5.11 on either side, nothing easy and nothing extreme. The climbing leans on balance, stemming and mantling, so footwork matters more than strength. It faces southwest and catches plenty of sun. The base is only about five minutes from the car, which makes it a handy stop for a quick session at altitude.
az_wind_wall.approach: About five minutes from the pullout just before the Windy Point lot, going around the west end of the wall to reach the base.

az_lebowski_wall.blurb: A bolted wall high on the hillside in the East Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, southeast of Tucson. All twelve climbs here are sport routes, running from 5.8 to 5.13 with the heaviest concentration in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Lines range from slab to steep and can be one to three pitches, with chain anchors. It is a good pick for climbers working through the 5.10s and 5.11s. The base is flat and roomy, the views over the valley are wide, and the wall gets shade by mid-afternoon after the morning sun.

az_breezeblocks_the.blurb: A cluster of boulders on a sunny hillside above Schnebly Hill Road east of Sedona, formed from one large block that has split into pieces. The twelve problems mix faces, aretes and cracks, from V0 up to the V5 range, with a good number of easy to moderate lines and a few hard ones at the top end. It works well as a winter destination and a breeze often moves through the blocks. Reaching it takes a drive up a rough road and a walk of roughly 20 to 45 minutes, so plan for a full session.

az_main_wall.blurb: The showcase wall of the Hog Heaven area in the McDowell Mountains, northeast of Phoenix, and the one that sits right beside the main trail. It faces east and rises close to 200 feet. All twelve climbs listed are trad, with a couple of easy 5.6 lines and then a strong run of 5.10s, plus two at 5.11. Several routes have a reputation for being mentally demanding. Expect a decent hike of roughly half an hour or more, and a quieter, less crowded scene than the better-known granite near Tom's Thumb.

_skipped.az_warm_up_wall_the: Only one page names this wall (a one-problem entry in West Kelly Canyon); no second page about it could be fetched.

_conflicts.az_breezeblocks_the: Stored rock is limestone, but both https://www.mountainproject.com/area/111491582/the-breezeblocks and https://www.mountainproject.com/area/110135684/sedona-bouldering describe sandstone (Schnebly Hill sandstone).
